ranking.rationale: Night vs day is a strong, semantically causal proxy for visibility, traffic behavior, and crash severity that should transfer across domains better than calendar fields or rare weather categories, while avoiding stronger domain/leakage signals like year.

Hour adds strong, broadly stable signal beyond night/day by capturing commute and traffic-pattern risk that should generalize across domains better than year, minute, rare weather categories, or location-proxy road attributes.

Rain is a direct, semantically causal hazard signal for accident severity/risk that should transfer across domains better than calendar variables or sparse location proxies. It adds complementary weather information beyond night and hour while avoiding stronger domain/leakage concerns from year, month, or post-event distance.

Visibility is a strong, semantically causal hazard signal for accident severity/risk that should transfer across domains. It complements already selected night, hour, and rain by capturing degraded seeing conditions beyond those proxies, while avoiding more domain-specific or leakage-prone cues like year or rare weather-category indicators.

Road-topology cues are typically stable across domains, and being near a junction is a strong, semantically causal indicator of accident severity/risk beyond already selected time-of-day and weather features. It adds robust structural information while avoiding brittle temporal/domain identifiers like Year or sparse weather one-hots.

Traffic signals add strong, semantically stable road-context information beyond time, weather, visibility, and junction status. They capture intersection control and conflict structure that should generalize across domains better than calendar variables, rare weather one-hots, or potentially post-outcome severity proxies like distance.

Crossing adds stable road-topology signal complementary to Junction and Traffic_Signal. It captures conflict points where vehicles and pedestrians intersect, which should remain predictive across domains without relying on brittle time/place identifiers or post-accident leakage.

Snow adds strong, semantically stable signal about hazardous driving conditions beyond rain, visibility, night, and road-structure features. It is more directly tied to accident severity/risk across domains than calendar variables or rare weather categories, and is less likely to act as a domain identifier than year/month or highly localized POI features.

Stop-sign presence adds complementary, semantically stable road-structure signal beyond junctions, crossings, and traffic signals. It is plausibly predictive of accident severity/risk across domains, less likely than calendar features to encode temporal domain shifts, and less brittle than rare weather-category one-hots.

Fog adds strong, semantically causal signal about hazardous driving conditions that should transfer across domains. It complements already selected visibility, rain, snow, night, and road-control features by capturing low-visibility risk not fully explained by those variables, while avoiding more domain-specific or leakage-prone calendar and location-surrogate features.

Directly captures active precipitation intensity, adding stable accident-severity signal beyond rain/snow/fog indicators and visibility. It is more semantically causal and less domain-specific than calendar fields, year, or rare weather-category dummies, and complements the already selected weather and road-context features.

Month adds stable seasonal structure beyond Hour and twilight, capturing broad shifts in daylight, road conditions, and weather-related risk without relying on brittle location or demographic proxies. It is likely more robust across whyshift domains than Year or sparse weather-category indicators, and less redundant than temperature or humidity given the weather features already selected.

Weekday adds stable behavioral exposure information beyond hour and month, capturing recurring commute and traffic-pattern differences that plausibly affect accident severity across domains. It is more semantically robust than year/day/minute, less redundant than additional weather one-hots, and less likely than rare road-feature indicators to encode brittle location-specific artifacts.

Temperature adds broad, semantically stable weather-risk signal beyond rain/snow/fog/visibility/precipitation, helping distinguish icing, heat, and seasonal road conditions without relying on domain-specific identifiers or sparse artifact categories.

Wind speed adds complementary, semantically causal weather-risk information beyond temperature, visibility, precipitation, and coarse weather categories. It should transfer across domains better than calendar granularity, rare weather one-hots, or POI/location proxies, while avoiding stronger leakage from accident extent or temporal/domain identifiers.

Humidity adds broadly stable weather-state information not yet captured by visibility, precipitation, temperature, wind speed, and coarse weather categories. It helps distinguish hazardous moisture conditions like damp air, mist, and icing risk across domains, while being less likely than year, minute, distance, or rare one-hot categories to encode domain-specific artifacts or leakage.

Roundabouts are a stable road-geometry/intersection-control signal that can affect accident severity and traffic conflict patterns across domains, while being less tied to temporal or regional distribution shifts than Year/Day/Minute or rare weather/wind categories. It adds complementary infrastructure information beyond Junction, Crossing, Stop, and Traffic_Signal without obvious leakage.

Traffic-calming infrastructure is a semantically meaningful road-design cue that should transfer across domains and adds complementary signal beyond junction/crossing/stop/traffic-signal by capturing speed-control context linked to accident severity/risk. It is less likely than year/day/minute or rare weather/wind one-hots to encode temporal or regional distribution artifacts, and more directly predictive than weaker POI indicators like amenity or station.

Cloudy weather adds broad, semantically stable signal about driving conditions beyond rain/snow/fog and existing continuous weather variables. It is more common and likely more useful out-of-domain than rare event categories, while avoiding temporal/domain-leakage features like Year and post-incident severity proxies like Distance.

Thunderstorms add distinct, semantically causal hazard information beyond rain, fog, snow, visibility, precipitation, and wind speed. This weather signal should transfer across domains better than year/day/minute or rare location/POI indicators, while avoiding stronger leakage risk from accident consequence features like distance.

Distance affected by the accident is a strong, semantically causal indicator of accident severity in WhyShift accident and should transfer across domains better than calendar identifiers, rare weather one-hots, or location-proxy POI features. It adds substantial signal not yet covered by the selected time, weather, visibility, and road-context variables, while avoiding especially brittle domain markers like Year.

Adds complementary severe-weather signal not fully captured by wind speed or other weather indicators; likely to remain semantically predictive across domains, while alternatives are either redundant, too sparse, weakly causal, or more likely to encode temporal/domain-specific artifacts.

Railway adds stable road-context signal not yet covered by junction/signal/crossing/stop features. It can meaningfully affect accident severity and traffic complexity across domains, while being less likely than year, day/minute, rare weather dummies, or wind-direction one-hots to encode temporal/domain shift or sparse brittle artifacts.

Road bumps are a stable, causal roadway-design cue for accident risk/severity that should transfer across domains better than calendar fields, rare weather categories, or wind-direction one-hots. It adds complementary infrastructure information beyond junctions, crossings, stops, signals, roundabouts, traffic calming, and railway, with low risk of acting as a domain or time identifier.
